name: SSD1351 1.5" 128x128 RGB OLED
description: Solomon Systech SSD1351 driver with a 1.5-inch 128×128-pixel colour OLED (65K colours in RGB565, or 262K) on a write-only 4-wire SPI bus with a data/command pin. The board has an RT9193 3.3 V regulator for the chip and an SX1308 boost converter that makes the 13 V panel supply, so VCC takes 3.3 V or 5 V, but the chip's logic runs at 3.3 V: drive it from 3.3 V GPIO only. Sold as: Waveshare 1.5inch RGB OLED Module (SSD1351, 128×128, 7-pin header VCC, GND, DIN, CLK, CS, DC, RST, plus the same signals on a PH2.0 cable socket).
eli5: A small, bright colour screen with no backlight: each pixel makes its own light, so black is truly black.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V or 5 V (RT9193 regulator to 3.3 V on the board; a boost converter makes the 13 V panel voltage)

pins.name: DIN
pins.description: SPI data in (MOSI, the chip's SDIN/D1); 3.3 V logic

pins.name: CLK
pins.description: SPI clock (the chip's SCLK/D0), at most 4.5 MHz; 3.3 V logic

pins.name: DC
pins.description: Data/command select: low = command, high = data (the chip's D/C#)

pins.name: RST
pins.description: Reset, active low (at least 2 µs low)

supplierQuery: 1.5 inch RGB OLED module SSD1351 128x128 SPI
buildNotes: VCC can be 3.3 V or 5 V (the board regulates it to 3.3 V), but DIN, CLK, CS, DC and RST go straight to the SSD1351, whose inputs are rated to VDDIO + 0.3 V (about 3.6 V). Drive them from 3.3 V GPIO (ESP32, Pico); never from 5 V logic.
Current is about 60 mA with the whole screen white and about 4 mA when black (Waveshare, at 3.3 V): an OLED draws power only for lit pixels.

Init order (datasheet + panel maker's example): RES# low ≥ 2 µs, wait 300 ms; FDh 12h and FDh B1h to unlock; AEh display off; B3h F1h; CAh 7Fh; A2h 00h; A1h 00h; A0h 74h (65K colour, RGB order, COM127→0); B5h 00h; ABh 01h; B4h A0h B5h 55h; C1h C8h 80h C8h; C7h 0Fh; B1h 32h; B2h A4h 00h 00h; BBh 17h; B6h 01h; BEh 05h; A6h; clear the RAM; AFh display on.
Drawing: 15h column start/end, 75h row start/end (one byte each, 0–127), then 5Ch and the pixels, 2 bytes each in RGB565, high byte first.
SPI mode 0, write-only (no MISO). The datasheet minimum 4-wire clock cycle is 220 ns, so keep the clock at 4.5 MHz or below (the example uses 4 MHz).
The BS resistor on the back must stay in the 0 (4-wire SPI) position; in 3-wire mode the DC pin is not used.

driver.code:
# SSD1351 1.5" 128x128 colour OLED (Waveshare 1.5inch RGB OLED Module), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the Solomon Systech SSD1351 Rev 1.5 datasheet and the panel's application example:
# 4-wire SPI (mode 0, MSB first, clock cycle >= 220 ns so <= 4.5 MHz), D/C low = command byte,
# D/C high = its parameters and pixel data. 65k-colour mode: RGB565, 2 bytes per pixel, high byte first.
from machine import Pin
import framebuf
import time

BLACK = 0x0000
WHITE = 0xFFFF
RED = 0xF800
GREEN = 0x07E0
BLUE = 0x001F
YELLOW = 0xFFE0
CYAN = 0x07FF

WIDTH = 128
HEIGHT = 128


def rgb(r, g, b):
    """24-bit colour -> RGB565."""
    return ((r & 0xF8) << 8) | ((g & 0xFC) << 3) | (b >> 3)


class SSD1351:
    def __init__(self, spi, dc, cs, rst=None):
        self.spi = spi
        self.width, self.height = WIDTH, HEIGHT
        self.dc = Pin(dc, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.cs = Pin(cs, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.rst = Pin(rst, Pin.OUT, value=1) if rst is not None else None
        if self.rst:
            # RES# low for at least 2 us resets the chip (datasheet 8.9 / Table 13-1).
            time.sleep_ms(1)
            self.rst(0)
            time.sleep_ms(1)
            self.rst(1)
        # Datasheet 8.9: wait at least 300 ms after VCI is stable before sending commands.
        time.sleep_ms(300)
        self._cmd(0xFD, b'\x12')  # command lock: unlock the MCU interface
        self._cmd(0xFD, b'\xB1')  # make A2/B1/B3/BB/BE/C1 accessible
        self._cmd(0xAE)  # sleep mode on (display off) while configuring
        self._cmd(0xB3, b'\xF1')  # front clock divider /2, oscillator frequency 0xF
        self._cmd(0xCA, b'\x7F')  # multiplex ratio 128
        self._cmd(0xA2, b'\x00')  # display offset 0
        self._cmd(0xA1, b'\x00')  # display start line 0
        # Re-map / colour depth 0x74: horizontal increment, column 0 -> SEG0, colour order C-B-A
        # (red in the top bits of RGB565), COM scan COM127 -> COM0, COM split odd/even, 65k colours.
        # Same orientation bits as the panel maker's example (0xB4), but 16-bit pixels.
        self._cmd(0xA0, b'\x74')
        self._cmd(0xB5, b'\x00')  # GPIO0/1 high impedance, input disabled
        self._cmd(0xAB, b'\x01')  # function selection: internal VDD regulator on
        self._cmd(0xB4, b'\xA0\xB5\x55')  # segment low voltage: external VSL
        self._cmd(0xC1, b'\xC8\x80\xC8')  # contrast current for colours A, B, C
        self._cmd(0xC7, b'\x0F')  # master contrast: full
        self._cmd(0xB1, b'\x32')  # phase 1 = 5 DCLKs, phase 2 = 3 DCLKs
        self._cmd(0xB2, b'\xA4\x00\x00')  # display enhancement
        self._cmd(0xBB, b'\x17')  # pre-charge voltage
        self._cmd(0xB6, b'\x01')  # second pre-charge period 1 DCLK
        self._cmd(0xBE, b'\x05')  # VCOMH 0.82 x VCC
        self._cmd(0xA6)  # normal display mode
        self.fill(BLACK)  # clear the RAM before switching on (panel power-up sequence)
        self._cmd(0xAF)  # sleep mode off (display on); SEG/COM come on within 200 ms
        time.sleep_ms(200)

    def _cmd(self, c, data=b''):
        self.cs(0)
        self.dc(0)
        self.spi.write(bytes([c]))
        if data:
            self.dc(1)
            self.spi.write(data)
        self.cs(1)

    def _window(self, x, y, w, h):
        self._cmd(0x15, bytes([x, x + w - 1]))  # set column address (start, end)
        self._cmd(0x75, bytes([y, y + h - 1]))  # set row address (start, end)

    def blit(self, buf, x, y, w, h):
        """Write w*h big-endian RGB565 pixels (2 bytes each) at (x, y)."""
        self._window(x, y, w, h)
        self._cmd(0x5C, buf)  # write RAM

    def fill_rect(self, x, y, w, h, colour):
        x, y = max(0, x), max(0, y)
        w, h = min(w, self.width - x), min(h, self.height - y)
        if w <= 0 or h <= 0:
            return
        self._window(x, y, w, h)
        line = bytes([colour >> 8, colour & 255]) * w
        self.cs(0)
        self.dc(0)
        self.spi.write(b'\x5C')
        self.dc(1)
        for _ in range(h):
            self.spi.write(line)
        self.cs(1)

    def fill(self, colour):
        self.fill_rect(0, 0, self.width, self.height, colour)

    def pixel(self, x, y, colour):
        self.fill_rect(x, y, 1, 1, colour)

    def text(self, s, x, y, colour=WHITE, bg=BLACK):
        """Draw text with MicroPython's built-in 8x8 font."""
        w = 8 * len(s)
        buf = bytearray(w * 8 * 2)
        fb = framebuf.FrameBuffer(buf, w, 8, framebuf.RGB565)
        # framebuf stores RGB565 low byte first; the SSD1351 wants the high byte first, so swap.
        sw = lambda c: ((c & 0xFF) << 8) | (c >> 8)
        fb.fill(sw(bg))
        fb.text(s, 0, 0, sw(colour))
        self.blit(buf, x, y, w, 8)

    def contrast(self, level):
        """Master contrast 0..15 (command C7h)."""
        self._cmd(0xC7, bytes([level & 0x0F]))

    def invert(self, on=True):
        self._cmd(0xA7 if on else 0xA6)

    def display(self, on=True):
        self._cmd(0xAF if on else 0xAE)  # sleep mode off / on

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import sys
import time
from ssd1351 import SSD1351, WHITE, YELLOW

# Pico: GP18/GP19 belong to SPI0. ESP32: any pins work on SPI(2).
spi_id = 0 if sys.platform == 'rp2' else 2
# SSD1351 4-wire SPI clock cycle >= 220 ns: 4 MHz is within the datasheet limit.
spi = SPI(spi_id, baudrate=4000000, polarity=0, phase=0, sck=Pin({CLK}), mosi=Pin({DIN}))
oled = SSD1351(spi, dc={DC}, cs={CS}, rst={RST})
time.sleep(1)
oled.text('SPARKBENCH', 24, 40, YELLOW)
oled.text('SSD1351 OK', 24, 60, WHITE)
print('drawn')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
